techDebt.planShipsOnTime: Hard-coding Colombia next to Mexico behind a country flag fits in one quarter. Taking on debt on purpose buys the date.
techDebt.planCountryFlags: Two countries switched by flags inside one checkout is more branches than the problem needs, and everyone can see them.
techDebt.planFitnessFunctions: A written plan, an ADR and two CI checks (no new country flags, checkout tests run per country) cost about a week of one team.
techDebt.planRepaymentQuarter: The quarter after launch, one team spends most of its time extracting a country seam instead of shipping features. The repayment is scheduled, so it actually happens.
techDebt.planDebtRetired: Once the seam exists and the fitness functions guard it, the flags come out and stay out.
techDebt.planLaunchEdgeCases: Some Colombian edge cases (tax IDs, address formats) slip past the shortcut; the per-country checks catch most of them within days, not all.
techDebt.planRegulatorReadsAdr: The regulator asks how country rules are controlled. A dated ADR and a repayment ticket are an answer, though not a free one.
techDebt.noPlanShipsFastest: No ADR, no checks, no seam: the shortcut ships a little faster than the planned one, because the plan was the only overhead.
techDebt.noPlanIfsEverywhere: Without a boundary, 'if country == CO' lands wherever someone needed it: pricing, tax, invoices, payouts.
techDebt.noPlanTribalKnowledge: The knowledge of where the Colombia branches live is in three people's heads, and the team has forty.
techDebt.noPlanInterestCompounds: Each new feature has to be written twice, once per country, and the shared tables gain country columns nobody owns. Interest is charged on every change.
techDebt.noPlanVelocityGone: Two quarters on, the velocity bought at launch has been paid back with interest. 'Later' never got a date.
techDebt.noPlanRegressions: Changes to the Mexican checkout break the Colombian one and nobody notices until a customer does. Code without tests is legacy the day it merges.
techDebt.noPlanLaunchBreaks: Launch week surfaces the cases nobody wrote down: peso formatting, tax IDs, a payout bank that rejects the file.
techDebt.noPlanRegulatorArchaeology: The regulator asks where country rules are enforced. Finding out takes an audit of the codebase, paid at consultant rates.
techDebt.generalQuarterLate: Extracting a country seam from a checkout that assumes Mexico takes the whole quarter: tests around the old code first, then the seam, then Colombia.
techDebt.generalEngineeringCost: A quarter of two teams spent on a refactor the business cannot see.
techDebt.generalBurnsRunway: Colombia's revenue starts a quarter later, about two months of runway spent waiting for it.
techDebt.generalSeamConcept: A country abstraction is a new concept every engineer must learn before touching checkout.
techDebt.generalCleanSeam: With one place where country rules live, adding Colombia is configuration, and the next country is cheaper again.
techDebt.generalFewerRegressions: Checkout tests run per country on every change; regressions in one market stop leaking into the other.
techDebt.generalMissesWindow: The launch date arrives and the checkout is not ready. Marketing was already spent, and part of the demand goes to a competitor that launched first.
techDebt.generalRegulatorOnePlace: Country rules live in one module with tests, so the regulator's questions have a short answer.
techDebt.colombiaOrders: Colombia adds roughly 1,200 orders a day in its first quarter, if the checkout can take them.
techDebt.colombiaSecondMarket: A second market means a second set of holidays, carriers, banks and support hours to keep in mind.
techDebt.licenceComplianceCost: A payments licence brings controls, reporting and the people to run them, whatever the architecture.
techDebt.licenceChangeControl: Licensed means change control: production changes in regulated flows need a record and a second approver.

tech-debt.title: Colombia by next quarter
tech-debt.concept: Technical debt as a deliberate decision with a repayment plan: Cunningham's metaphor, Fowler's quadrant, seams and fitness functions.
tech-debt.voice: Every codebase has debt. Some of it has a payment schedule.
tech-debt.briefing: Forty engineers, and the business wants Colombia live in one quarter. The checkout assumes Mexico in the currency, the tax IDs, the addresses and the payouts. There is a shortcut, and everyone already knows where it goes.
tech-debt.dilemma: Do you borrow the quarter, and if you do, who writes down when it gets paid back?
tech-debt.disagreement: Experts disagree here. Cunningham's original metaphor only works if you repay by refactoring, and many argue debt without a plan is just a mess with a nicer name. Others point out that most debt is discovered, not chosen, and that a repayment plan written under deadline pressure is mostly optimism. Both have seen it happen.
tech-debt.readNext: Read Cunningham's short experience report for what the metaphor originally meant, then Fowler's quadrant to tell prudent from reckless, then Feathers on seams and the fitness-function chapters of Building Evolutionary Architectures for how to make the repayment stick.

shortcut-with-plan.title: Take the shortcut, on purpose, with a repayment plan
shortcut-with-plan.optimizes: Colombia on the date; the debt has an owner, a deadline and two CI checks guarding it.
shortcut-with-plan.costs: A week of plan and checks now, and a whole quarter of repayment that ships nothing visible.

shortcut-no-plan.title: Take the shortcut and pay the debt when it hurts
shortcut-no-plan.optimizes: Colombia on the date, without spending a week planning to repay a debt that may never be worth repaying.
shortcut-no-plan.costs: Interest on every change after, and nobody decides when it hurts enough.

generalize-first.title: Generalize the checkout first, launch a quarter late
generalize-first.optimizes: A country seam that makes Colombia, and the next country, cheap and safe.
generalize-first.costs: The launch date, part of the demand and two months of runway.

events.colombia-launch: Monday, 09:00 Bogotá time. Colombia is live. The first order is paid in pesos; the right ones, hopefully.
events.regulator-licence: The payments licence is granted, with conditions. The first one: show us where each country's rules are enforced.

inspections.checkout-cracks: Site inspection: hairline cracks along the checkout, branching wherever someone wrote 'if country'. Measured, dated, and either scheduled for repair or not.

review.which-quadrant: Is this debt deliberate or inadvertent, prudent or reckless, and what about the situation made it so?
review.what-interest: What interest does this decision pay, on which part of the system, and who pays it?
review.when-repaid: When does the debt get repaid, what triggers the repayment, and how would you notice it slipping?

rubric.grounded-context: The context names the constraints that actually shaped the choice (team, launch date, orders, regulation).
rubric.names-debt-kind: The decision says whether debt was taken, and whether on purpose.
rubric.names-tradeoff: The consequences name at least one force that got worse, not only the ones that got better.
rubric.names-given-up: What was given up is written down in a full sentence.
rubric.repayment-plan: The revisit section is a repayment plan with a trigger or a date: what gets refactored, by when, and what check enforces it.
